summary: S. 2806, titled the Eliminate Shutdowns Act, sets up an automatic funding mechanism to prevent government shutdowns when regular fiscal year appropriations bills have not been passed before a new fiscal year begins. It provides temporary funding in 14-day increments at the rate of operations from the prior fiscal year.

affected_groups.effect: Receive automatic temporary funding in 14-day increments based on prior-year operational rates to keep functioning during a funding gap.
affected_groups.group: Federal agencies, programs, projects, and activities experiencing a lapse in appropriations

key_provisions: Provides automatic continuing appropriations in 14-day intervals if a full-year appropriation act has not been enacted before a fiscal year begins.
Sets funding at the rate of operations provided in the preceding applicable appropriation act.
Allows agency heads, with Office of Management and Budget approval, to transfer up to 5 percent of any appropriation account to a higher-priority account under specific conditions.
Restricts automatic funding from being used to initiate or resume any program, project, or activity specifically prohibited during the previous fiscal year.
Specifies that programs with high initial rates of distribution to states, foreign countries, or grantees cannot make those full distributions if they would impinge on final funding prerogatives.
missing_information: The exact total cost or fiscal impact of the automatic appropriations.
Specific details on which individual agencies or non-federal entities might be impacted by grant distribution restrictions.
summary_detail.plain_summary: S. 2806, titled the Eliminate Shutdowns Act, sets up an automatic funding mechanism to prevent government shutdowns when regular fiscal year appropriations bills have not been passed before a new fiscal year begins. It provides temporary funding in 14-day increments at the rate of operations from the prior fiscal year.
summary_detail.significance: The bill changes how federal funding gaps are handled by establishing an automated fallback mechanism to prevent government shutdowns, maintaining prior-year spending levels temporarily while Congress works on regular appropriations.
